display_name_comment: S.GN_L is the name the pedal shows (descriptor name entry only). effect_name SGNL is used for the file (SGNL.ZDL), the C symbol and the SONAME, because '.' is not legal in a C name. If the pedal shows the name wrongly or refuses the effect, delete display_name and rebuild: the effect is then simply called SGNL.
comment: S.GN_L - a broken digital line: the sound is cut into packets and some never arrive, like a VoIP call on bad Wi-Fi or a DAB radio losing lock. Loss = how many packets are lost; Size = packet length (2 to 100 ms: short = buzz and grit, long = stutter); Codec = codec quality going down (spectral holes, low-pass, lower sample rate, fewer bits); Fill = what replaces a lost packet (GAP silence, REPT replays the last packet, FADE replays it dying away, NOISE hiss, REVRS backwards, GARBL corrupted data, LATE out-of-order packets, RND a random one per outage, never GARBL); Burst = scattered single losses or long outages; Jump = sudden quality drops; Line = band of the line (HIFI, VOIP, PHONE, WALKY); Edge = hard clicks or soft ramps at the packet edges; Mix is a DJ-style dry/wet crossfade.
gid_comment: 0x08 = Delay category -> Fx_DLY_. Grouped under DLY with the rest of the pack.
fxid_comment: 480 DualShft, 485 DubSiren, 486 Choral, 487 WaveFold, 488 EuGate, 489 S.GN_L (this pack). Unique inside the repo; check other community effects.

params.name: Loss
params.comment: How many packets are lost. 0 = clean line, 100 = about 85 % of the packets lost. Default 30 (about 13 %).

params.name: Size
params.comment: Packet length, 2 ms to 100 ms (shown in ms). Short packets turn losses into grit and, with Fill REPT, a robotic buzz at the packet rate (5 ms = about 200 Hz); long packets make syllables and notes drop out or stutter. Default 40 (about 10 ms).

params.name: Codec
params.comment: Codec quality going down: random spectral holes (the underwater MP3 sound), a closing low-pass, a lower sample rate and fewer bits, all on one knob. 0 = clean. Above 50 the first packet after a silence is lost too, like a call clipping the start of a word. Default 30.

params.name: Fill
params.comment: What replaces a lost packet. GAP = silence; REPT = the last packet that arrived, replayed over and over (buzz or stutter); FADE = the same replay dying away over about 30 ms; NOISE = soft hiss at the level of the sound; REVRS = the last packet backwards; GARBL = corrupted data, boosted random slices held for random lengths; LATE = out-of-order packets, each lost packet plays a random older one; RND = each outage picks one of the others at random, except GARBL. Default REPT.

params.name: Burst
params.comment: How the losses are grouped, with the same overall amount. 0 = single scattered losses, 100 = long outages (about 12 packets on average). Default 30.

params.name: Jump
params.comment: How often the codec suddenly drops to a much worse quality for a few packets and comes back, like a stream changing bitrate. 0 = never. Default 20.

params.name: Line
params.comment: Band of the line, before the codec. HIFI = full band; VOIP = 200 Hz to 5 kHz, steep low cut, boxy headset bump at 1.5 kHz; PHONE = 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz; WALKY = 500 Hz to 2.5 kHz, a bit driven. Default HIFI.

params.name: Edge
params.comment: Shape of the cut where a packet is lost or comes back. 0 = hard clicks (authentic), 100 = soft fades that fill most of the packet (they grow with Size). Default 30.

params.name: Mix
params.comment: Dry/wet crossfade, DJ style: dry full up to 50, wet full from 50, both full at 50. 100 = only the broken line, 0 = only the original.

audio_nop_comment: Set true for a UI-only smoke build before trusting the DSP.
